statement: The attainable real-bitangent-line counts are 4, 8, 16, and 28. Respectively the six real quartic topologies (four ovals; three ovals; two nonnested ovals; one oval; two nested ovals; empty) have 28,16,8,4,4,4 real bitangent lines.

answer.text: The attainable real-bitangent-line counts are 4, 8, 16, and 28. Respectively the six real quartic topologies (four ovals; three ovals; two nonnested ovals; one oval; two nested ovals; empty) have 28,16,8,4,4,4 real bitangent lines.
answer.qualification: Real bitangent lines; contact points need not both be real. Tropical totally-real lifting results have additional hypotheses.

scope: Real bitangent lines to a smooth real plane quartic; tangency points may be real or a complex-conjugate pair.
notes:
This includes real lines tangent only at conjugate nonreal points; it is not the spectrum of totally real tangency. The theorem is explicitly credited to classical work by Zeuthen and Klein.

Originality audit: the real classification is attributed to Zeuthen; Plaumann–Sturmfels–Vinzant is the modern verification source retained in source. Minimum/maximum counts are consequences of that classification. Original Zeuthen text has not been directly checked here.
